unit.why: A framed exemplum about R. Mordechai Yaffe (the Levush), excommunicated in Venice by his Sephardi teacher for not answering Amen; it contains an embedded tale of a Spanish pious man executed by a king, followed by a homiletic and halakhic exhortation on answering Amen.
unit.boundary_note: Homiletic discussion of answering Amen continues into the next division (quote from Or ha-Yashar).

stories.start_quote: לאהבת אחי ורעי אספר לפניכם מעשה
stories.end_quote: ואני מוחל לך אבל בתנאי שתדרוש ברבים להזהירם על עני׳ אמן
stories.summary_en: R. Mordechai Yaffe goes to Venice to learn the calendar from the Sephardi sage Abuhav. He fails to answer Amen to the sage's child's blessing and is excommunicated. The sage then tells him of a Spanish pious man whom a king had dismembered for missing Amen to a priest's blessing; the man later revealed in a dream that this was punishment for once not answering Amen to his own son. The sage's condition for forgiveness is that the tale be preached everywhere.

tags.why: Concerns the pre-Hasidic Levush and Sephardi sages

tags.why: The narrative is wrapped in an extended homiletic and halakhic exhortation
